title: The Typewriter of the Lower Danube Anew
premise: In 1946, Oscar Winterbourne hides in a Danube river town under a borrowed name, the last courier of a republic that no longer exists, carrying coded documents he was ordered to destroy but never did. When Ilse Brandt—the woman he promised in peacetime to protect, believed dead—arrives alive and hunted as an enemy collaborator, his carefully constructed invisibility collapses. To honor his promise, Oscar must decode the documents, expose the man who betrayed them both, and choose between erasing himself forever or testifying and losing everything. He testifies; Ilse escapes downriver on the last barge of autumn while Oscar, stripped of his alias but finally owning his name, begins rebuilding a life that is genuinely his own.
about_author: T. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records along the Danube corridor. The Typewriter of the Lower Danube Anew is their second novel, drawn from letters found sewn into a courier's coat lining.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar Winterbourne, living as clerk 'Anton Reiter' in a 1946 Danube port town, keeps meticulous false ledgers by day and burns one page of his true past each night. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the suffocating comfort of deliberate anonymity, and the first crack—a letter arrives addressed to a name only the dead should know.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: The letter is in Ilse Brandt's unmistakable hand—the woman Oscar promised to protect in peacetime and mourned for two years. A stranger named Kovac delivers it with a warning: she's alive, hiding upriver, and someone is closing in. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief inverted into vertigo; hope feels more dangerous than despair.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Oscar travels upriver under cover of a grain shipment, narrating flashbacks to the embassy's final days and the promise made in a garden before the shelling began. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: memory as both burden and compass; he realizes he kept the coded documents not from duty but from guilt.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: In a flooded mill, Oscar finds Ilse—changed, sharp, distrustful, passing as a widow. She reveals the documents name her protector-turned-betrayer, Major Voss, now a rising official in the new administration. POV: alternating Oscar and Ilse. Emotional beat: two people relearning intimacy through suspicion; the promise becomes a debt neither can refuse.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Twice
chapters.summary: Oscar decodes enough of the documents to see Voss signed orders under both regimes, selling names to survive each transition—including Ilse's family. But using the papers means revealing himself. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: rage sharpened into strategy; she refuses to run again and forces Oscar to stop calculating his own safety.

chapters.title: Kovac's Price
chapters.summary: Kovac, their smuggler-ally, is exposed as a double agent feeding Voss information; he offers Oscar a trade—Ilse's location for Oscar's clean exit papers. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable; survival has always been Oscar's religion, and it demands exactly this betrayal.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Oscar feeds Kovac false coordinates while moving Ilse toward the river barges, but Voss's men raid the mill early; a chase through reed marshes ends with Kovac dead and the documents half-lost to the water. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: terror and clarity fused—the moment Oscar stops being a courier and becomes a witness.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Oscar surrenders to the Allied commission, revealing his true identity and presenting what remains of the decoded pages, knowing it destroys his alias and exposes him to reprisal. POV: Ilse, waiting. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full; identity reclaimed at the cost of safety.

chapters.title: Voss in the Dock
chapters.summary: At the hearing, Voss dissects Oscar's record—desertion, concealment, complicity—but Ilse appears unbidden, corroborating the signatures with testimony that risks her own indictment. Voss falls. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph; justice arrives muddy, partial, and human.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Autumn's last barge carries Ilse downriver to a new life; Oscar, nameless no longer, chooses to stay and work the commission's archives, restoring other people's stolen names. They part at the dock with a promise renewed, not repeated. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—survival transformed into purpose, memory into inheritance.
